name: Memphis International
subtitle: Stand assignment and push control for the FedEx World Hub ramps
source: Stand numbers, lead-in lines, headings, taxiways, aprons and buildings from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): each stand 20 m back from the nose end of its lead-in line (half way along on the short feeder lines). Where an OSM lead-in has no number, it takes the number of the X-Plane Scenery Gateway KMEM startup location on it (2024); five unnumbered lead-ins at the west edge are W1-W5 (north to south) and two at the southwest corner SW1-SW2 (west to east), names of our own. Layout checked against Esri World Imagery and the user's Google Maps screenshot of the FedEx ramp. Where OSM and the Gateway number the same lead-in differently (the 500 row, 557/558, and the 850s/860s that OSM numbers 950s/960s), OSM wins. Generated frame: north up, 1.5 m/px, linear in lat/lon.

positions.name: FedEx Ramp
positions.note: No ramp frequency is given, so the stand telex has no CTC line.

buildings.name: Memphis Air Route Traffic Control Center

airlinesSource: FedEx (FDX) and flights with FEDEX in remarks park on the hub ramps; the 900s feeder pads are offered last. Other operators are not given out automatically.
notes: FedEx World Hub stands, numbered as in OpenStreetMap: 100s east, 200s along the International Sort, 300s north of it, 400s-600s around the original sort, 700s-800s west and the center column, 900s the northwest feeder pads.
W1-W5 and SW1-SW2 are unnumbered lead-ins; the names are ours.
No ramp frequency is given, so telexes carry no CTC line.
